title: Interception of registration data in transit reveals identity
description: The registration flow carries directly identifying and highly sensitive personal data (email, name, government ID) plus authentication secrets (password, six-digit code). If the transmission is observable in transit, the parent can be identified and profiled.
assumptions: Applies if transport confidentiality/integrity protections are absent, weak, misconfigured, or bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact subnode may differ in the canonical threat tree.

title: Linkability via repeated registration-flow metadata
description: Even if payload contents are protected, metadata of the registration flow such as source IP, device/browser fingerprint, timing, and repeated submissions can allow linking multiple attempts to the same parent or household.
assumptions: Assumes network or application-layer metadata is observable or logged and can be correlated across submissions.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree subnode may vary; grounded in metadata-based linkability on the flow.

title: Detectability of a parent's registration attempt
description: The mere occurrence of this flow may reveal that a specific individual is attempting to register for the service, even without reading the full contents. Traffic patterns, endpoint access, or observable message characteristics can disclose this event.
assumptions: Assumes an observer can see that communication with the authentication service occurs.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; detectability is inferred from observable communication existence.

title: Excessive collection of personal data during registration
description: The authentication service receives a broad set of personal data for registration, including government ID, name, email, password, and a six-digit code. Collecting a government ID at account creation may exceed what is necessary for authentication if not strictly justified, creating a data minimization risk.
assumptions: Assumes government ID is not strictly necessary for this registration purpose or that less intrusive alternatives exist.
uncertainty_note: Necessity depends on business, legal, or age/guardian verification requirements not provided in the prompt.

title: Unawareness about registration-data use and retention
description: On receipt of the registration data, the authentication service may process or retain the parent's email, name, government ID, and code without the parent being adequately informed about purposes, retention periods, sharing, or mandatory versus optional fields.
assumptions: Applies if privacy notices, just-in-time explanations, or consent/notice mechanisms are missing, unclear, or incomplete at registration.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side unawareness risk inferred from the collection context; exact notice design is not described.

title: Registration data processed without a valid legal basis or beyond stated purpose
description: The authentication service may collect and process sensitive registration attributes, especially government ID, without an appropriate legal basis, or may later use them for purposes incompatible with account registration and authentication.
assumptions: Assumes legal basis, purpose limitation, and necessity have not been established or documented for all collected fields.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and service context; exact legal assessment is outside the provided facts.

title: Parent can later deny having submitted the registration data
description: Because the source is an external user submitting registration details, insufficient evidence of submission, notice acceptance, or verification steps could allow the parent to repudiate having sent specific data or initiated registration.
assumptions: Applies if the system lacks adequate submission records, verification logs, or confirmation mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Included as a plausible privacy-relevant repudiation issue for this flow; exact applicability depends on audit and confirmation design.

title: Excessive storage of parent account data in users collection
description: Storing the parent account in the MongoDB users collection may disclose more personal data than is necessary if the full parent profile, unnecessary attributes, or long-lived account details are persisted rather than the minimum fields needed for authentication and account management.
assumptions: Assumes the stored parent account contains personal data and that some fields may not be strictly necessary for this datastore's purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is based on best judgement for unnecessary collection/storage under Data Disclosure; exact node wording may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Parent account records may be linkable across contexts
description: If the users collection stores stable identifiers such as email address, phone number, external identity IDs, or shared account keys, records about the same parent can be linked across services, sessions, or datasets beyond what is necessary for authentication.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers are stored in the parent account record and may be reused across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node may differ; applicability depends on whether persistent identifiers are stored.

title: Stored parent account data may enable identification
description: The users collection may contain directly identifying attributes or combinations of attributes that allow a parent to be identified from the stored account record.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account includes identifiers such as name, email, phone number, address, or unique account identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement node selection; the flow description is brief and does not enumerate fields.

title: Stored account attributes may reveal sensitive facts about a parent
description: Even if the purpose is authentication, the stored parent account may disclose private information through account metadata, recovery details, role information, family relationships, or other attributes retained in the users collection.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account schema includes metadata beyond a bare credential reference.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure here is interpreted as detectability/inference of personal facts from the stored record; applicability depends on schema richness.

title: Parent account data may be stored for unspecified or incompatible purposes
description: If the users collection stores parent account data without clear purpose limitation, the data may later be used for analytics, profiling, support, or other secondary purposes not expected from the original authentication interaction.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation and retention/use constraints are not strictly enforced at the datastore.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on governance and purpose controls, which are not described in the flow.

title: Insufficient notice or consent for storing parent account details
description: If parents are not adequately informed that their account data will be stored in the MongoDB users collection, or if storage includes optional fields without an appropriate legal basis, the processing may occur without valid awareness or consent where required.
assumptions: Assumes some stored fields may require explicit notice or consent depending on jurisdiction and legal basis.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on the system's notices, legal basis, and whether optional or sensitive fields are stored.

title: Excessive disclosure of user attributes to the parent
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the payload includes more attributes than are necessary for the parent-facing purpose, the source process causes unnecessary disclosure of the child's or account holder's personal data to an external entity.
assumptions: Assumes the parent does not need all included user attributes for the immediate transaction and that some attributes may relate to another data subject (e.g., child account data).

title: Identity information exposed in transit via JWT or accompanying user data
description: The flow carries a JWT and user data to an external entity. If the token or payload contains directly identifying claims or stable identifiers, interception or unintended observation of the flow can reveal the identity of the authenticated user or related data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection, token encryption, or payload minimization may be absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Applies particularly if JWT contents are readable bearer tokens rather than opaque references; tree-node id is approximate.

title: Linkability through stable identifiers in the JWT
description: A JWT commonly contains stable claims such as subject identifiers, account ids, tenant ids, or session-correlating metadata. These can allow the parent user, intermediaries, or observers to link multiple interactions or datasets to the same user across sessions or services.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT or accompanying user data includes persistent identifiers or consistent metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate because detailed node mapping was not provided in context.

title: Parent can plausibly deny receipt or use of the token and user data
description: Once the JWT and user data are delivered to the external parent user, there may be insufficient evidence that the recipient actually received, viewed, or used them. This can hinder accountability for downstream privacy-relevant actions performed with the token or data.
assumptions: Assumes no reliable receipt logging, acknowledgment, or binding of token use to the recipient.
uncertainty_note: This is a weaker threat than disclosure/linkability and depends on accountability requirements in scope; tree-node id is approximate.

title: Insufficient transparency to the parent about JWT contents and downstream processing
description: The parent user may receive a JWT and user data without clear notice about what personal data the token contains, how long it remains valid, what systems will process it, or what privacy consequences follow from sharing or storing it. This creates non-compliance risk around transparency and informed processing.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or notice does not adequately explain token contents, purposes, retention, and sharing implications.
uncertainty_note: Included only insofar as this flow is user-facing and transparency obligations attach to what is delivered to the external entity; tree-node id is approximate.

title: Credentials and parent email can identify the child account if intercepted in transit
description: The login flow carries a parent email address and password from the child user to the authentication service. If the transmission channel is observable or insufficiently protected, the parent email directly identifies the associated family/account and the credential payload can be tied to a specific child login attempt.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may be exposed to network observers through missing or weak transport protection, or through observable metadata around the request.

description: Even if only limited content is visible, repeated authentication requests on this flow may allow an observer to correlate multiple login attempts to the same account or household using stable identifiers such as the parent email, endpoint patterns, timing, or other communication metadata.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker or intermediary can observe repeated instances of this flow or related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node id is approximate; linkage via communication metadata is the main concern.

title: Child may be unaware that a parent's email is being disclosed during login

uncertainty_note: This is a plausible detectability/awareness issue at the source, but applicability depends on the actual UI and notices.

title: Authentication service may be unable to prove or disprove who initiated the login attempt
description: Because the flow contains shared family credentials (parent email and password), the authentication service may later be unable to distinguish whether the login was initiated by the child, the parent, or another person with access to those credentials. This can undermine accountability for privacy-relevant actions tied to authentication events.
assumptions: Assumes credentials may be shared within a household or otherwise not uniquely bound to one natural person.

title: Authentication service could use login credentials for secondary purposes beyond authentication

title: Video-stream metadata can link sessions to the same child
description: Metadata on the streaming flow, such as persistent session identifiers, IP address, device identifiers, CDN tokens, or repeated request patterns, can allow observers or intermediaries to link multiple viewing sessions to the same child or household.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries stable or quasi-stable identifiers or observable traffic patterns.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Streaming traffic may identify the child or household
description: Identifiers or distinctive network metadata in the video stream delivery path may enable an observer, intermediary, or delivery partner to identify the child user or their household, especially when combined with subscriber, device, or network records.
assumptions: Assumes the stream is not fully anonymized and that delivery infrastructure can observe account-, device-, or network-level identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not provide detailed I threat-tree nodes.

title: Receipt of the stream exposes viewing choices on the child's device
description: Once the stream reaches the child user's device, local recipients or nearby observers may detect what content the child is consuming from on-screen playback, notifications, cached titles, or playback history, revealing personal preferences or habits.
assumptions: Assumes the external entity includes the child's device/environment and that local observation is in scope for destination-side privacy effects.
uncertainty_note: Destination-side detectability depends on whether local observation of the external entity is considered within scope.

title: Streaming may involve improper personal data management
description: Delivering the video stream may entail processing personal data such as child account identifiers, viewing history, parental-approval status, device identifiers, and delivery logs. If the service sends or retains more data than necessary for playback, or lacks an appropriate legal basis/transparency for child-data processing, the flow can contribute to non-compliance.
assumptions: Assumes child-related identifiers, approval context, or playback logs are processed as part of streaming.

title: Excessive disclosure of child browsing data to recommendation engine
description: The childprofiles collection may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary when sending browsing data to the AI Recommendation Engine. Because the data concerns children and browsing behavior, unnecessary attributes, historical depth, or identifiers could create avoidable exposure beyond what is needed for recommendation generation.
assumptions: Assumes the planned flow includes raw or richly detailed child browsing data rather than a minimized feature set.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may differ in the canonical tree.

title: AI processing may use child browsing data for purposes users do not expect
description: On receipt, the AI Recommendation Engine may analyze child browsing data in ways that are not transparent or reasonably expected, such as profiling, model training, or secondary optimization purposes beyond immediate recommendation delivery. This creates an unawareness threat, especially given the sensitivity of children's data.
assumptions: Assumes purposes, model behavior, retention, or downstream uses are not fully explained to children/guardians.
uncertainty_note: Exact U subnode is inferred from standard LINDDUN unawareness concepts; retrieved context did not provide the detailed threat tree.

title: Use of child browsing data by AI engine may lack valid consent or appropriate child-data legal basis
description: Processing child browsing data in the AI Recommendation Engine may occur without sufficiently specific, informed, and verifiable consent from a parent/guardian, or without another appropriate legal basis and child-specific safeguards. If the AI use is newly planned, the original collection basis may not cover this downstream processing.
assumptions: Assumes the AI recommendation purpose is new or materially different from the purpose for which the browsing data was originally collected.
uncertainty_note: Applicable legal basis depends on jurisdiction and system context; tree-node id is best judgement.

title: AI engine can link browsing data to an identifiable child profile
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may be able to link incoming browsing data to a persistent child profile, account, household, or device identity. Even if direct identifiers are limited, stable profile keys or correlated behavioral patterns can enable linkage across sessions or datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the flow contains persistent identifiers, profile keys, or sufficiently distinctive behavioral records.
uncertainty_note: Specific linkage mechanism is not described in the prompt, so applicability depends on actual schema and identifiers sent.

title: AI engine may infer sensitive attributes about the child from browsing behavior
description: By processing browsing history or browsing-derived features, the AI Recommendation Engine may infer interests, vulnerabilities, age-related traits, health concerns, emotional state, or other sensitive characteristics about the child that were not explicitly provided. This increases privacy risk beyond the original data disclosed in the flow.
assumptions: Assumes the recommendation model derives latent traits or segments from behavioral data.
uncertainty_note: Inference risk is strong for behavioral recommendation systems, though the exact inferred attributes are context-dependent.

title: Unnecessary disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine plans to share users' browsing data with third-party advertisers. This is a cross-boundary transfer of personal data to a third party and may exceed what is strictly necessary for providing recommendations, creating an avoidable disclosure risk under the data-minimisation principle.
assumptions: Browsing data relates to identifiable or reasonably linkable users and is not strictly necessary to be sent to advertisers for the core service requested by the user.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for explicit third-party disclosure/minimisation; exact sub-node naming may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Third-party advertisers can link browsing data with existing advertising profiles
description: Upon receipt, advertisers may combine the browsing data with their own identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, or existing customer records, enabling cross-context linkage of the user's activity and profile enrichment.
assumptions: Advertisers possess independent identifiers or datasets that can be matched to the received browsing data.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; applicability of linkability at the destination is high given the recipient is an advertiser.

title: Browsing data may enable identification by advertisers
description: Even if the shared browsing data is not overtly identifying on its own, advertisers may use it together with account data, tracking identifiers, IP-derived information, or other datasets to identify the individual behind the browsing behavior.
assumptions: The transferred browsing data contains persistent identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or sufficiently distinctive behavioral patterns.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; identification depends on the granularity and identifiers present in the browsing data.

title: Advertisers can infer sensitive interests or attributes from browsing data
description: Browsing histories and interaction patterns can reveal or strongly suggest sensitive topics, preferences, health concerns, political interests, religion, sexuality, or other private attributes when analyzed by advertisers.
assumptions: Browsing data includes URLs, page categories, search/referral context, timestamps, or similar signals rich enough for profiling.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; detectability/inference risk is strongly supported by the nature of browsing data.

title: Secondary advertising use may be unexpected by users
description: Users may not reasonably expect browsing data collected for recommendations to be repurposed and shared with third-party advertisers. This creates an unawareness threat if the sharing and downstream advertising use are not transparent and understandable to users.
assumptions: The planned sharing is not prominently disclosed in context, or users would not naturally expect this transfer from the service interaction.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; unawareness depends on the quality and timing of notice presented to users.

title: Sharing browsing data with advertisers may be incompatible with consent or purpose-limitation requirements
description: Sending browsing data to third-party advertisers may lack a valid legal basis, exceed the original purpose for which the data was collected, or violate consent/preferences if users did not specifically agree to advertising disclosure and profiling.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy requires a specific legal basis, purpose limitation, and/or opt-in consent for third-party advertising uses of browsing data.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate and compliance depends on jurisdiction, consent design, and contractual arrangements.

title: Collection and storage of full government ID images may exceed data minimization
description: The Authentication Service sends full government ID images to backend/uploads/ for storage. Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data and often contain more attributes than are strictly necessary for authentication. If storing the complete image is avoidable, this flow causes unnecessary disclosure by collecting and persisting more personal data than needed.
assumptions: Assumes the service could achieve its purpose with less data, e.g. extracted attributes, redacted images, or short-lived processing instead of persistent storage.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement for explicit, avoidable disclosure/minimization; retrieved context did not provide a more specific Dd subtree citation.

title: Sensitive ID images may be disclosed in transit on the internal flow
description: This flow transfers government ID images from the Authentication Service to the file system. If the transfer path, transport mechanism, or operational logging exposes the payload or file metadata, the images could be disclosed during transit beyond what is necessary for the intended processing.
assumptions: Assumes the write path may traverse components, APIs, mounts, queues, or logs where payloads or filenames are observable.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on implementation details of how P1 writes to DS4; if this is a strictly local in-memory write with no observable transit, this threat may be less relevant.

title: Persistent storage of government ID images in uploads directory may enable avoidable disclosure
description: Once received, the File System stores government ID images in backend/uploads/. Persistent storage in a general uploads location can expose the images to administrators, backup systems, other services, or later secondary uses, creating avoidable disclosure if long-term retention or broad accessibility is not strictly required.
assumptions: Assumes DS4 is persistent storage and that retention, backup, or access scope may exceed the minimum necessary for identity verification.
uncertainty_note: Specific subtree citation is approximate; the core issue is destination-side avoidable disclosure through storage/retention and access scope.

title: Storing raw ID images may be non-compliant with purpose limitation and retention obligations
description: Government ID images are commonly subject to strict legal and policy constraints. Receiving and storing them in the file system may violate purpose limitation, storage limitation, or special handling obligations if the system lacks a defined lawful basis, retention schedule, or safeguards appropriate for identity documents.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy or sectoral rules constrain storage duration, purpose, and protection of identity-document images.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and business context, so this is a plausible but context-dependent non-compliance threat.

title: JWT in localStorage enables cross-context linkability on the device
description: Storing a persistent JWT in browser localStorage can let scripts running in the same origin reuse the same token across sessions and application contexts, making user actions linkable over time. If multiple parts of the application or embedded scripts access the token, they can correlate requests and behavior to the same user/browser.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is stable long enough to act as a persistent identifier and is accessible to application scripts in the origin.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: JWT stored in localStorage can identify the user or browser
description: A JWT commonly contains claims or an opaque identifier that uniquely identifies the authenticated user or browser session. Once stored in localStorage, any script with origin access can read it and use it to identify the user directly or indirectly.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains identifying claims or is usable as a unique reference to backend identity.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; applicability is strong.

title: JWT contents in localStorage may disclose personal data
description: JWTs often embed claims such as subject identifiers, roles, email addresses, tenant identifiers, or other attributes. Persisting the token in localStorage risks disclosure of those claims to any script executing in the origin, browser extensions, shared-device users, or forensic access to the browser profile.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted and contains readable claims beyond a meaningless random reference.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure severity depends on actual JWT contents and client environment.

title: Users may be unaware that authentication tokens persist in localStorage
description: Persisting a JWT in localStorage can create hidden session persistence beyond what users expect. Users may not understand that closing the tab or browser may not remove the token, reducing their ability to manage logout, shared-device use, or residual authentication state.
assumptions: Assumes the application does not clearly communicate token persistence and lifecycle to users.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement node id.

title: Storing JWT in localStorage may conflict with data-minimization and secure-storage expectations
description: Using localStorage for authentication tokens can be unnecessary or excessive from a privacy/compliance perspective when less exposed mechanisms exist, such as short-lived tokens held in memory or HttpOnly secure cookies. The storage choice may undermine compliance with privacy-by-design, storage limitation, and appropriate technical safeguards obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy/security requirements that expect proportionate protection for authentication data.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction, policy baseline, and available alternatives.

title: Excessive disclosure of child history to the parent
description: When Child Profile Management retrieves and sends child history for review, it may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the parent's immediate purpose, such as full historical records, sensitive events, or data about third parties embedded in the history.
assumptions: Assumes the child history can contain sensitive or extensive records and that not all retrieved fields are strictly necessary for each parent review action.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed disclosure subnodes.

title: Identification of the child or family via data in transit and metadata
description: The content of the child history, or metadata on the flow such as account identifiers, timestamps, and routing context, may directly or indirectly identify the child, parent, or household if observed or exposed during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted payload or accompanying metadata contains direct identifiers or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Specific transport protections are not described, so applicability depends on whether transit exposure is plausible.

title: Linkability through recurring identifiers and history metadata
description: Recurring identifiers, account references, device/session metadata, or stable child-profile attributes in this flow could allow observers or intermediaries to link multiple history retrieval events to the same child or family over time, enabling profile building.
assumptions: Assumes repeated requests or responses carry stable identifiers or distinguishable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Applies mainly if network-visible metadata or payload fields remain stable across transactions.

title: Further disclosure by the parent after receipt
description: Once the parent receives the child history, the information may be exposed beyond the intended context, for example through shared devices, screenshots, forwarding, or viewing by unauthorized household members.
assumptions: Assumes the parent endpoint or environment may be shared or insufficiently private.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side privacy threat contingent on the parent's environment and application controls.

title: Lack of awareness about scope and sensitivity of disclosed child history
description: The parent may not be adequately informed about what categories of child history are being shown, why they are available, how current they are, or any restrictions on further sharing, reducing transparency around the disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly explain the provenance, scope, or handling expectations for the history data.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement node selection due to missing detailed knowledge-base node mapping for non-compliance/transparency.
